$comment: [X2.4] GitHub MCP attach spec. Tier-1 first-party-ms (GitHub = MS subsidiary, own verified org identity per X1.4). Shape === mcp-specs/_template.json (X2.1). CC0-1.0.
title: GitHub Repository Operations
description: GitHub repository, issue, pull-request, and Actions operations via the official GitHub MCP server.

env_vars.name: GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN
env_vars.description: GitHub personal access token (classic or fine-grained) — the token env name the reference MCP server reads. Scopes the operations the server can perform; pass via env, never inline in args (doctrine #6).

env_vars.name: GITHUB_TOKEN
env_vars.description: Alternate token env name (e.g. CI `github.token`); use either GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN.

env_vars.name: GITHUB_PAT
env_vars.description: Alternate token env name accepted by the server.

auth.recipe: set GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN to a personal access token; fine-grained tokens scoped to the target repos are preferred over classic. CI may pass the Actions `github.token` as GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN.

sample_tools.name: get_file_contents
sample_tools.summary: Read a file from a repository.

sample_tools.name: list_pull_requests
sample_tools.summary: List pull requests on a repository.

known_limitations: Requires a valid GITHUB_TOKEN; without it the server attaches but all repo-scoped tools return an auth error.
Tool capabilities are bounded by the token's scopes — a read-only token cannot create issues or PRs.
Destructive-action audit (X2.18): branch/file deletion tools are flagged in `destructive_tools` and are blocked when the trust policy sets `allowDestructive: false`.

client_install.claude_desktop: Add to claude_desktop_config.json mcpServers as `github`: { command: npx, args: [-y, @modelcontextprotocol/server-github], env: { GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN: "<token>" } }.
client_install.cursor: Settings → MCP → Add: name `github`, command `npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-github`; set GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN in the env.
client_install.vscode: Add to .vscode/mcp.json servers as `github` (VS Code Insider, MCP preview); supply GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN via inputs.
